title: Opportunity Vetting and Release Credit System for Strategic Accounts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem statement: Strategic/enterprise customers frequently request guaranteed runway (timed delivery windows) or scope reservations. We currently accept asks via ad-hoc channels (account teams/AMs/SEs) which causes scope slippage, unclear commitments, and an opaque load on engineering sprints. Objective: Build a lightweight Opportunity Vetting + Release Credit System (OVRCS) that lets PMs, sales, and AEs 1) vet requests against value/effort, 2) allocate a consumable pool of release credits to top accounts, and 3) simulate runway impact on upcoming cycles so stake-holders can make informed trade-offs.
mvp_scope:
- Intake form template (Confluence + AE submit UI) with required fields: business impact, expected MRR/ARR impact, data sensitivity, compliance needs, timeline preference.
- Release credit ledger: admin UI + simple API to allocate/consume credits per account. Credits map to sprint weight (e.g., 1 credit = 3 story points equivalent).
- Runway simulator: visualization in Console showing the effect of credit reservations on next 3 cycles (capacity vs committed credits).
- Vetting rubric: objective scorecard and automated recommendation (accept / defer / partial scope) exposed to PM/AE.
- Lightweight audit trail and customer-facing acknowledgement template.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intake submissions create a ledger entry and appear in the vetting queue.
- PM/Eng can allocate/adjust credits and the ledger updates in real-time.
- Runway simulator accurately reflects sprint capacity based on release credit-to-point mapping and flags overloads > 80%.
- Vetting rubric produces consistent recommendations for a sample set of 25 historical asks (>=80% alignment with historical decisions).
- Audit trail logs user, timestamp, and decision note for every allocation (retention 90 days).
success_metrics:
- Decrease ad-hoc VIP escalations to PM Slack channel by 60% in first 2 cycles after rollout.
- Time-to-decision on top-account requests reduced from median 7 days to <=48 hours.
- <10% of reserved credits result in unfulfilled commitments due to capacity mis-estimation after 3 cycles.
stakeholders: Arjun Rao - Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Accounting for variable sprint velocity (holidays/on-call) will cause overcommit. Mitigation: start with conservative credit-to-point mapping and include a slack buffer in simulator.
- Risk: Sales teams may game the scoring. Mitigation: require finance sign-off for high-value credit grants and periodically audit allocations.
- Risk: Increased operational overhead for PMs. Mitigation: phased rollout (pilot with 3 accounts) and automation for low-effort vetting flows.
tradeoffs:
- Depth vs speed: We can build a richer scoring engine (ML/score weighting) but that delays delivery. For MVP we use deterministic rules and a manual override.
- Guaranteed runway vs flexibility: Allocating credits formally commits capacity; we recommend partial credits for longer-running asks to preserve flexibility.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Pilot, 4 weeks): Manual intake + ledger CSV + runway simulator with sample data for 3 pilot accounts (AMs/SEs).
Phase 1 (Alpha, 8 weeks): Admin UI + API + vetting rubric + pilot with 10 accounts.
Phase 2 (Beta, 12 weeks): Public AE submit UI + Console integration + audit logs + reporting + limited GA to top 50 accounts.
Phase 3 (GA): Full rollout + SLA playbook + training and playbook for customer success and sales.
